current_date: 2024 (Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024; Newcastle's copy is dated Jan 25) - not verified by this audit
current_evidence: This audit could not fetch anything: the shared WebFetch budget (400/hour) and the per-turn WebSearch budget had both run out. The current-list details come from the sibling Gateshead audit in this run. It found the joint 'Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024' still linked on Gateshead's page, and the Newcastle copy states 'This latest document supersedes the validation checklist published in 2019'. Grokbot's North Tyneside extract carries 2024-list content (BNG Schedule 7A text, Note 39 CIL), so the North Tyneside page probably presents the same current list, but this was not confirmed.

issues.detail: List date and Date basis are blank, and 'Outdated (>2y)?' says 'Undated'. The joint Tyneside list is the 2024 checklist, which supersedes the 2019 Tyne and Wear list. The date should be recorded as 2024, or January 2025 for the Newcastle-hosted revision.
issues.evidence: Sibling Gateshead audit: 'Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024' ... 'This latest document supersedes the validation checklist published in 2019'.

issues.detail: Householder 'Coal Mining / Land Stability Risk Assessment' is placed under Householder, but Grokbot's own excerpt says householder extensions are exempt.
issues.evidence: '...required for development in Coal Mining Development High Risk Areas with the exception of householder extensions or alterations, changes of use and shop front alterations.'

issues.detail: Several rows under 'Change of use - prior approval' use triggers that exclude change of use or apply to planning applications rather than GPDO prior approvals. 'Block plan / Site plan' excludes change of use only. 'Landscaping scheme' excludes wholly change of use/conversion. 'Structural Survey' covers planning applications to convert rural buildings. The 'Flood Risk Assessment' row's 'change of use' wording refers to planning applications for change of use.
issues.evidence: '(i.e. excluding applications for change of use only...)'; 'other than wholly change of use/conversion applications'; 'The change of use or conversion of rural buildings (e.g. barn conversions)'.

issues.detail: Reserved matters is shown as '(none)', yet Grokbot's own Sustainability Statement trigger names major reserved matters applications. Separately, about 33 Full planning rows carry the note 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. Examples are Air Quality, Archaeology, BNG, Open Space, Telecoms, Viability and Waste Management Plan. Many of these also apply to outline, reserved matters or householder schemes, depending on thresholds. Outline has only a Travel Plan row, and its excerpt does not name outline at all.
issues.evidence: 'Sustainability Statement When is this required? Major full planning applications and major reserved matter applications.'

issues.detail: Several requirement labels carry another requirement's text. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' and 'Construction (Environmental) Management Plan' both carry the SuDS Construction Method Statement text. 'Lighting Assessment' carries the daylight/sunlight proximity-to-windows trigger. 'Daylight / Sunlight / Overshadowing' carries a list of metrics plus wind-tunnel text, with no trigger. 'Planning Obligations / S106 Heads of Terms' carries BNG obligation text.
issues.evidence: Trigger excerpts in app_type_rows, e.g. Schedule of works = 'A Construction Method Statement for the proposed SuDS...'.

issues.detail: Many triggers are cut-off fragments, document-title rules or definitions rather than the actual threshold. Examples: 'Design and Access Statement' = 'Design and Access Statement (if required) 8.'; 'Arboricultural Impact Assessment' = '...will be required (see section 35).'; 'Archaeological Assessment' = 'When is this required? Archaeological desk based assessment Proposals on or near Scheduled Monuments;' (cut off); 'Marketing' = 'conservation areas Marketing information will not always be required.'; 'Foul Sewage' and 'Sequential / Exception Test' carry only 'The title must state...' and the 3-year age rule; 'Affordable Housing Statement' carries what-to-include questions with no unit threshold; 'Transport Assessment' carries the definition of a Transport Statement; 'CIL' carries introductory text; 'Travel Plan' (Outline) carries a garbled table header.

Some triggers quote clauses that apply only to the other Tyneside councils and are misleading on the North Tyneside tab. 'Contaminated Land' quotes the simple screening rule for single dwellings 'Within Gateshead, Newcastle and South Tyneside'. 'Health Impact Assessment' quotes the Gateshead-only HIA thresholds. The tab_item listing 'Newcastle and Gateshead Core Strategy Policies... South Tyneside Core Strategy...' is likewise another council's policy list.
issues.evidence: 'Within Gateshead, Newcastle and South Tyneside , in applications for single dwellings...'; 'In Gateshead , Health Impact Assessments (HIA) will be required for...'

issues.detail: Several items are not validation requirements. 'Employment / Economic Statement': the source says it is not required for validation. 'Pre-application advice / engagement details': its trigger is table-of-contents text. Six of the 11 tab_items are boilerplate: 'Failure to submit the required information...', 'LINKS TO SUPPORTING GUIDANCE DOCUMENTS ... MAY BE SUBJECT TO CHANGE' plus data protection, 'paper copies ... not recommended', 'signatures already redacted', 'Confidential- Not for Public Use', and the Core Strategy policy list.
issues.evidence: '...submit an Economic Statement ... but this would not be required for validation purposes.'; 'Checklists (v) Pre-Application Advice (vi) Local Authority Contact Details Appendix 1...'

issues.detail: Grokbot's Gateshead extraction of the same joint 2024 checklist has these requirements, but North Tyneside has no row for them. (1) Drainage Strategy / SuDS (major development). (2) Acoustic and Vibration Assessment, required where development may create noise or is noise-sensitive. (3) Planning Statement. (4) Tall buildings / wind microclimate assessment. (5) Minerals safeguarding assessment (non-mineral development over 1ha). (6) Heritage at Risk / photomontages. (7) Landscape strategy/masterplan and landscaping details for major/full schemes. The landscaping row exists only under change of use. The sibling audit also reports these as absent: Overheating Assessment and Mitigation (Note 26); Heritage Statement for major schemes in conservation areas and for demolition in conservation areas (Note 19); and Ecological Impact Assessment for non-householder schemes affecting habitat (Note 16). Full planning has no Ecology row and no Heritage Statement row.
issues.evidence: Comparison of Grokbot app_type_rows, Gateshead (2024 source) vs North Tyneside; sibling audit: 'contents list Note 26 Overheating Assessment and Mitigation Requirements'.

issues.detail: 'Floor plans / Elevations' and 'Existing and proposed site levels / sections' share one identical trigger. 'Construction Management Plan' and 'Schedule of works' share the SuDS text. The HRA appears both as a tab_item and as a Full planning row with the same fragment.

This audit could not fetch the live source because the shared WebFetch budget and the per-turn WebSearch budget were exhausted. Every issue above therefore comes from Grokbot's own extracted text and from Grokbot's Gateshead extraction of the same joint list. Specific thresholds and missing items should be re-checked against the 2024 Tyneside checklist.
issues.evidence: Proxy: 'web-fetch budget for this session is exhausted: 400 per hour, shared by every agent'.

summary: The live source could not be fetched because the web budgets were exhausted, so contents were not checked against it. The joint Tyneside 2024 checklist is probably what the link shows, but the workbook leaves it undated. Grokbot's own extracts show misplaced triggers, Householder coal mining and change-of-use rows that the source excludes, boilerplate counted as requirements, and several joint-list requirements missing (SuDS, acoustic, planning statement, tall buildings, minerals, overheating).
